I'm on a roll with these questions this weekend. Anyway:

10 - Warhammer 40K DoW Dark Crusade - Where DoW's campaign stopped being shit and started being amazing.

9 - Warhammer 40K DoW Soulstorm - They took Dark Crusades campaign and gave it steroids. 'Nough said.

8 - Team Fortress 2 - The amazing FPS with a twist that involved OP as hell weapons and the stranges classes around bursting with personality.

7 - Cities Skylines - What Sim City could have been but better.

6 - Borderlands 2 - Borderlands 1 was good but I have a few issues with it that doesn't allow me to put it here. Borderlands 2 however is a excellent game which is very cheap and a hell of a lot of fun.

5 - Spore + Expansions - People say this game was nowhere near what it could have been. But for what it is I still love this game heavily and recommend it to everyone. Don't listen to those who say this game sucks. It's one of the most joyful gaming experiences I've ever had.

4 - Kerbal Space Program - Mods + Space + Reverse talking + Little green men + Hilarity = This game. It's the steam summer sale too you have NO reason to pick this game up.

3- Roller Coaster Tycoon 1 - The start of a very successful game genre. Singlehandedly programmed by the godly Chris Sawyer in assembly with more detail than most games today.

2 - Roller Coaster Tycoon 3 Platinum - Considered by many to be the worst of all 3 RCT games so far. I disagree. the 3D graphics and fairly easy UI makes it very easy for anyone to pickup. The modding community as well means you can never run out of ideas.

1 - Roller Coaster Tycoon 2 - They took RCT1 and made it better in every single way. I grew up on this game and have played this more than all 9 other games on this list combined. Nearly 13 years later this game still holds up with people still creating beautiful parks which you well never get tired of. I can not recommend this game enough and insist that everyone reading this list goes and buys this game now. Everything about it is amazing. Did I mention it's also programmed in assembly by Chris Sawyer again?
Try to create a list of 10 games you believe everyone should own and why.

Super Mario Bros. - NES Because, even if it is not the pinnacle of 8-bit gaming, it is one of the most influential titles ever made. And more importantly it's still good. How many games more than thirty years old can still inspire new generations of game developers?

Portal. - PC One of the tightest, most enjoyable puzzle games ever made. It's simply fun to play. It's fun to solve the puzzles, it's fun to be mocked while solving puzzles, it's just a perfect example of a game that ends right when it should.

Dark Souls. - PC A masterpiece of level and world design (Lost Izalith and Bed of Chaos excepted), a punishingly difficult game that is also never unfair (except maybe the Carpa Demon), with a unique multiplayer system that only enhances the horrorful and dreadful atmosphere of the world.

Half Life 2 - PC IMO still one of the best shooters ever made. Others might be slightly better, but it's only by standing on the shoulders of this giant. A beautiful game with the perfect mix of action, pacing and plot.

The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past - SNES Some people might choose Ocarina of Time, but for me the best Zelda game is ALTTP. Two worlds to traverse, plenty of items, a ridiculous amount of secrets, puzzles, combat, bosses, and the music. To me, this is still what Zelda games, and action adventure games, have to live up to.

Super Metroid - SNES. Another pinnacle of the genre, this is the game without which the genre might not exist as it's known today. Symphony of the Night gets a lot of praise but, as with Half Life 2, it's only by doing what Super Metroid did years before that it's as good as it is. From the exciting opening aboard the Space Station Ceres, to the atmospheric trek through a familiar Brinstar on planet Zebes, to that final confrontation with Mother Brain and the Baby Metroid, this is a game that is so superbly designed it's still played today in competitive speed-runs.

Tetris - Game Boy. The ultimate puzzle game. It's pure simplicity is that it is immediately playable by anybody, with the goal instantly understood. You stack blocks to make lines, and then the lines disappear. A puzzle game that could not exist except digitally, and the game that sold a hundred million Game Boys.

Counter Strike: Global Offensive. - PC It's hard to pick one competitive FPS to put on a list, but for me it would be this one.

Starcraft: Brood War. - PC The grand-daddy, high-water mark of real time strategy. Starcraft 2 is good, but it's Brood War that does it for me.

Your favourite game. - Whatever "How could you leave blahblah off a list?" This is your joker, your wild card, your whatever. Don't bitch at me for not including obscure-import-only-PCE16-title here. Or put in Mario Party 8 for the Wii, because it's still a ridiculously fun drinking game.
